title: On Nodding to the elders first
subtitle: 人际沟通 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 人际沟通（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·人际沟通与交流）
meta: 主题语境：人际沟通（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·人际沟通与交流）　|　核心词汇：nod　|　正文 337 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 nod 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1949 the foreman ① nodded to the elders first on the same day, and every worker in the site said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three shifts on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the foreman ② nods to the elders first before dawn without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ nod to the elders first at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ nodded to the elders first before — a line in the sheet for May 1943 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Nodding to the elders first on the same day, the foreman said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the rope at the far ramp, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ nod off twice before supper before dawn, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Nod off twice before supper at once and never mention it again.

By 1956 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the sheet, and a new worker from the next site ⑧ nods off twice before supper on the same day every shift without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the ramp, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ nodded to the elders first again when nobody else would.

⑩ To nod to the elders first, my mother said in 1961, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the site remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the site forgets, somebody nods to the elders first before dawn again and somebody must nod to the elders first on the same day all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 点头（一般过去式 nodded to the elders first：1949 年工头头一回这样做，当天就）
B. v. 点头（一般现在 nods to the elders first：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 点头（不定式 to nod to the elders first：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 点头（过去完成时 had nodded to the elders first：1943 年五月的施工单上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 点头（动名词 nodding to the elders first 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 打盹（nod off twice before supper：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去打盹晚饭前打了两次盹）
G. v. 打盹（nod off twice before supper：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 点头（后段两处：新来的工人照例 nods off twice before supper，而母亲又一次 nodded to the elders first）

items.q: to nod to the elders first
nodded to the elders first before
nod off twice before supper before dawn
nod off twice before supper at once
nods off twice before supper on the same day
nodded to the elders first again
to nod to the elders first

answers.why: nod 意为“点头”，1949 年工头当天就点头先向长辈点头致意，那是工地里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 nodded。
nod 意为“点头”，自那以后工头天没亮就把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 nods。
nod 意为“点头”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯点头先向长辈点头致意”，此处为不定式 to nod to the elders first。
nod 意为“点头”，施工单里 五月 那行字说明早在 1956 年之前就有人点头过，故用过去完成时 had nodded。
nod 意为“点头”，工头说“点头先向长辈点头致意这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 nodding to the elders first 作主语。
nod 意为“打盹”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去打盹晚饭前打了两次盹”，should ever 之后用原形 nod off twice before supper。
nod 意为“打盹”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻打盹晚饭前打了两次盹（nod off twice before supper at once），以后再也不要提起。
nod 意为“点头”，新来的工人每个班次都照例打盹晚饭前打了两次盹，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 nods。
nod 意为“点头”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次当天就点头先向长辈点头致意，用一般过去式 nodded 叙述。
nod 意为“点头”，结尾那句是母亲 1961 年的话：要点头先向长辈点头致意，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和工地记住的那一件。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1949 年，工头当天就点头先向长辈点头致意；工地里每一个工人都说这是头一回。（nodded to the elders first）
多年以后，工头仍天没亮就做着同一件事，不必有人开口。（nods to the elders first）
母亲后来说，难就难在肯点头先向长辈点头致意这件事本身。（to nod to the elders first）
早在 1943 年就有人点头先向长辈点头致意，五月那天施工单上的一行字就是证据。（had nodded to the elders first）
工头说过，当天就点头先向长辈点头致意这件事，是九分耐心一分胆气。（nodding to the elders first 作主语）
老手们留下的规矩说得明白：立刻打盹晚饭前打了两次盹，以后再也不要提起。（nod off twice before supper，祈使句）

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 nod 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1949 the foreman nodded to the elders first on the same day, and nobody in the site forgot it.
Even now the foreman nods to the elders first before dawn whenever the site asks.
Nodding to the elders first on the same day, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever nod off twice before supper before dawn, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new worker from the next site nods off twice before supper on the same day every shift, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother nodded to the elders first again, and the site remembered that half.
